items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: and, uh, uh, Raleigh, uh, the Dixie Clubers.

ctx.x: Well I'll tell you how it's what, if he'd have it, when he'd be working he'd call us to get something, he'd call us Don't Touch Nuthin' for a second, fifth a time. You understand? I see. Well that's his men, he'd get them in together and then they'd get it. So you'd be working with other bands at the same time? I'd be working with, in fact I'd be working with many bands. And when I was working with him, I'd be working with Joe Howard and, uh, and, uh, and, uh, uh, Raleigh, uh, the Dixie Clubers.

I'd be working with Joe Howard and, uh, I'd be working with Joe Howard. Joe Howard was a leader? Yeah. What did he play then? How? He played trumpet. Did he play trumpet? Yeah. Now, uh, let me see. You must have been in your twenties by now, huh? Well I'm in five years, I don't know. Yeah, it's hard to keep it all strange. Well, who are you? Well, about England.
